title: Keep Mac awake to prevent sleep
summary: Use the caffeinate command to stop your Mac from going to sleep. You can keep it awake indefinitely, for a set time, or while a specific task runs.

steps.explain: Run caffeinate with the -d flag to prevent the display from sleeping. The Mac will stay awake until you stop the command.
steps.expect: The command runs in the foreground. Your Mac will not go to sleep.

alternatives.explain: Prevent sleep for a specific duration in seconds (e.g., 3600 for 1 hour) using the -u and -t flags.
Prevent idle sleep while a specific command (like 'make') is running using the -i flag.

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: The command to run while keeping the Mac awake.

alternatives.explain: Prevent sleep until a specific process ID finishes using the -w flag.

placeholders.name: PROCESS_ID
placeholders.description: The PID of the process to wait for.
